name: Back Extension Machine
instructions: Adjust the seat and the foot platform so the pad sits across your upper back and your hips line up with the machine's pivot. Sit with your feet on the platform and your back against the pad.
Cross your arms over your chest or hold the handles, and lean slightly forward to start with a long, neutral spine.
Press back against the pad by extending at the hips and lower back until your torso is in line with your hips. Do not lean back past a straight line.
Pause briefly, then return slowly to the start under control. Use a weight you can move smoothly without jerking.
image_prompt_scene: Side view of one person seated on a commercial back extension machine at the start of the movement, torso flexed forward, arms crossed on the chest. The seat is in front, a flat foot plate under the feet. Behind the person, a swing arm hinged at the machine frame next to the seat extends upward along the person's back and ends in a cylindrical roller that presses against the upper back at shoulder-blade height. The arm is clearly angled forward from its hinge, showing that it swings with the person. Nothing touches the lower back. No pads on the legs.
